privacy.heading: Privacy Policy
privacy.intro: Short version: this site runs no analytics, no ads, and no tracking. The only personal data it ever touches is what you type into the contact form yourself — plus a few settings your own browser remembers for you.
privacy.dontDo.heading: What this site does not do
privacy.dontDo.body: No Google Analytics, no tracking pixels, no ad scripts, no fingerprinting. Nothing about you is sold or shared, and no profile is built from your visits — there is simply nothing here watching you.
privacy.host.heading: Hosting and DNS
privacy.host.body: The pages themselves are static files served through Cloudflare, which necessarily sees your IP address and basic browser details to deliver them — the same as any host or CDN. I run no Cloudflare analytics on top of that.
privacy.bot.heading: Spam protection
privacy.bot.body: The contact form is protected by Cloudflare Turnstile, which loads only on the contact page — most visitors never see a challenge. To confirm the check, your browser talks to Cloudflare and shares your IP address with them. I store nothing from this step; all I ever receive is a yes or a no.
privacy.form.heading: Sending me a message
privacy.form.body: The form asks for your name, email address, and message. A Cloudflare Worker validates the submission, applies a short-lived rate limit, and forwards it to my inbox through Resend's email API — so Resend necessarily handles the message in transit. It is never written to a database on this site, and your email address is used for exactly one thing: my reply to you.
privacy.music.heading: Music data
privacy.music.body: The footer teaser and the /now page can show my latest listens from Last.fm. The lookup runs on the server, so your data is never involved — but album artwork loads directly from Last.fm's image servers, which see a normal image request from you. No account, no cookies, no tracking on my side.
privacy.terminal.heading: Terminal console
privacy.terminal.body: The optional terminal runs entirely in your browser: commands act on your device, navigation stays in your tab, and nothing you type is sent anywhere or remembered.
privacy.storage.heading: What your browser remembers
privacy.storage.body: A few small values stay in your own browser so the site remembers your choices. They never leave your device, and clearing site data removes every one of them:
privacy.storage.theme: theme — keeps your light or dark choice
privacy.storage.lang: lang — keeps the language you picked
privacy.storage.layout: layout — keeps your column width choice
privacy.links.heading: Links to other sites
privacy.links.body: Some links point outward — GitHub, LinkedIn, live projects. The moment you click through, their privacy policies apply instead of this one.
privacy.rights.heading: Your data, your call
privacy.rights.body: Nothing here is stored in a way I can't undo. If you want to know what was sent, or want a message deleted, just ask — email works too.
privacy.changes.heading: Changes to this page
privacy.changes.body: If anything here changes, this page and the date at the top change with it.

colophon.heading: Colophon
colophon.intro: A colophon is a note on how a book was made. This is that note for this site: the tools it is built with, and the people whose work lit the way. The list is honest but incomplete — many more developers shaped this site than I can name.
colophon.rowFrameworkBody: Astro 7 with Content Collections. Static pages in two languages — English at bare paths, Indonesian under /id/ — with hover prefetch and no client JavaScript by default.
colophon.rowStylingBody: Tailwind CSS v4 over design tokens; Newsreader for headings, Geist for UI, JetBrains Mono for code and labels.
colophon.rowLanguageBody: TypeScript throughout, checked strict — content schemas included.
colophon.rowBackendBody: One Cloudflare Worker serves the contact API and the Last.fm now-playing proxy, with KV rate limits; Turnstile stops the spam, Resend delivers the mail.
colophon.rowContentBody: Notes in Markdown and MDX, an RSS feed, a sitemap, and a Markdown twin of every page for machines.
colophon.inspirationBody: Many people shaped this site. These are some of them — and there are many more developers whose sites I can no longer name.
resume.tagline: Full-stack web developer who ships — from ad-tech SDKs to live products.
resume.profileBody: I'm Rafif, a full-stack web developer and IT undergrad at Universitas PGRI Semarang. I build web applications end to end: the products I create are live, the SDKs are dependency-free, and the automation I write runs real ad campaigns. I care about small, fast, maintainable systems — and I finish what I start.
resume.exp1.body: Designed and shipped an anonymous song-messaging app: a React + TypeScript frontend with animated delivery, an ElysiaJS API on Cloudflare Workers, Supabase and Postgres storage. Live today, from first sketch to deploy.
resume.exp2.body: Built a B2B ad-network SDK and telemetry backend for HTML5 web games. The client SDK is a single dependency-free TypeScript file under 8 KB served over CDN; the Node backend records impressions and clicks in SQLite running in WAL mode, deployed with Docker.
resume.exp3.body: Run day-to-day operations for a live browser-game portal: uptime, content flow, and the security side — honeypot fields and request validation that keep bots and scrapers off the platform.
resume.exp4.body: Wrote the automation tooling behind the studio's ad campaigns: the scripts that prepare, publish, and track creatives, so the marketing loop runs without manual busywork.
resume.exp5.body: Helping build a pure-heuristics CLI that scores Indonesian scam messages 0–100 — phishing, fake APKs, OTP traps, brand-lookalike domains. No runtime dependencies, tested with pytest, linted and CI-checked.
resume.exp6.body: Design-to-deploy websites for clients: scoping, building, and shipping full-stack apps end to end — then staying around for fixes and iterations.
resume.skillBackendBody: Node.js, ElysiaJS, Express, PostgreSQL, SQLite, Supabase
resume.skillInfraBody: Cloudflare Workers, Docker, Linux, Git, GitHub Actions
resume.educationBody: B.Sc. in Informatics (in progress), Universitas PGRI Semarang. Web development and systems design, self-taught through shipped projects — every technology above earned its place in production, not in a tutorial.
resume.cta: Available now for work, internships, or collaboration. The fastest way to reach me is the contact form — I reply to every serious inquiry.
